plants.name: Lupinus texensis
plants.description: Roadsides and rolling meadows turn deep blue-violet as bluebonnets fill the Texas Hill Country. Each flower spike is crowded with pea-like blooms. The upper petal carries a small white patch that fades to magenta as the flower ages.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late March to mid-April, with peak bloom usually in early to mid-April
plants.location: Central Texas and the Hill Country, USA
plants.funFact: The white spot on a young bluebonnet flower turns reddish-purple after pollination. This signals to bees that the flower has already been visited.

plants.name: Tulipa (garden hybrids)
plants.description: Rows of tulips stripe the Dutch bulb fields in bands of red, yellow, pink and orange. Their cup-shaped blooms open on bright mornings. Mid-April is when the fields and Keukenhof gardens are usually at their best.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late March to mid-May, usually at their best in mid-April
plants.location: Bulb-growing region of the Netherlands, including Lisse and Keukenhof
plants.funFact: Tulips came to Europe from Central Asia by way of the Ottoman Empire. In the 1630s, their prices in the Netherlands soared in the speculative frenzy known as Tulip Mania.

plants.name: Nerine bowdenii
plants.description: As the southern hemisphere moves into autumn, this bulb sends up sturdy, leafless stems. Each is topped with a spray of ruffled, shimmering pink flowers. Their narrow, wavy-edged petals sparkle in the light.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late summer to autumn, January to May in its native range
plants.location: Mountain grasslands and rocky slopes of South Africa, including the Drakensberg region
plants.funFact: The petals have a glittering, sugar-dusted look. This comes from the cell structure of the petal surface, which catches the light.
